title: Infinitesimal comparison with the graph of an etale closed subscheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $A$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $w_1,\ldots,w_m,y_1,\ldots,y_r\in A$, with $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\mathbf A_k^{m+r}$ etale [def-weil-field, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space]. Let $h_1,\ldots,h_s\in A$, $D=A/(h_1,\ldots,h_s)$, and $q:A\to D$ the quotient map [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Suppose that $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\mathbf A_k^m$ given by the images of $w$ is etale. Let $L/k$ be a field extension and $\epsilon:D\to L$ a $k$-algebra homomorphism. Suppose given $k$-algebra homomorphisms
$$\tau:A\to L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m,Y_1,\ldots,Y_r]],\qquad\sigma:D\to L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m]]$$
whose constant terms are $\epsilon q$ and $\epsilon$, and with $\tau(w_i)=\epsilon q(w_i)+W_i$, $\tau(y_j)=\epsilon q(y_j)+Y_j$, and $\sigma(q(w_i))=\epsilon q(w_i)+W_i$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Define $\phi_j=\sigma(q(y_j))-\epsilon q(y_j)\in(W)L[[W]]$. Then
$$\tau(c)(W,\phi(W))=\sigma(q(c))\quad(c\in A),$$
and $\phi$ is the unique vector $\psi\in(W)L[[W]]^r$ for which $\tau(h_i)(W,\psi(W))=0$ for every $i$. The comparison also holds after localizing $A$ and $D$ at the primes defined by the evaluations, since the denominators have nonzero constant coefficient. For every extension $L\hookrightarrow K$, applying it coefficientwise to $\tau,\sigma,\phi$ gives the same comparison and the unique solution over $K$. The integers $m,r,s$ may be zero; there is no closed-point hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 04FF (lemma-unramified-flat-formally-etale), with Definition 02HG (definition-formally-etale). Agent consequence of repeated unique lifting through the square-zero kernels (W)^q/(W)^(q+1), parent steps 4 and 5 and the graph-solution portion of step 11.

proof.text: For a zero-constant vector $\psi$, Mathlib MvPowerSeries.hasSubst_of_constantCoeff_zero makes substitution by $(W,\psi)$ an algebra homomorphism. Subtract the constant power series from an arbitrary series and apply constantCoeff_subst_eq_zero to see that this substitution preserves its constant coefficient. These constructions work for every finite number of variables, including zero.

Use the ring-level formally unramified predicate [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-ring-iff-kahler-zero]. If $e:P\to B$ is formally unramified and $f,g:B\to F[[W]]$ agree on $P$ and on constant coefficients, regard both as $P$-algebra homomorphisms, with the target algebra structure induced by $f e$. The power-series ring is Noetherian and local (Mathlib MvPowerSeries.isNoetherianRing and its local-ring instance). The constant-coefficient kernel is a proper prime ideal, hence is contained in the maximal ideal. Krull intersection [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson], specialized by Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isLocalRing, says its powers have zero intersection. Algebra.FormallyUnramified.ext_of_iInf therefore gives $f=g$. This Mathlib theorem performs the nilpotent-lifting induction and separation of the original plan. For an etale coordinate map $k[Z]\to B$, RingHom.Etale.formallyUnramified supplies the formal unramifiedness, and MvPolynomial.algHom_ext checks agreement over $k[Z]$ from agreement on the coordinates.

Put $q:A\to D$ and $\phi_j=\sigma(q(y_j))-C(\epsilon(q(y_j)))$. Its constant coefficients vanish by the hypothesis on $\sigma$. Apply step 2 to the coordinate map $k[W,Y]\to A$ and the maps $S_\phi\tau$ and $\sigma q$. Step 1 and the hypotheses give the same constant coefficients, while substitution on $C(a)$ and $X_i$ and the coordinate formulas show equality on $w$ and $y$. Thus $S_\phi\tau=\sigma q$, and evaluating at each $h_i$ gives zero. For uniqueness, $S_\psi\tau$ annihilates the span of the $h_i$ by Ideal.span_le and hence descends through Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ to $\rho:D\to L[[W]]$. Use step 2 for the etale coordinate map $k[W]\to D$: the maps $\rho$ and $\sigma$ agree on the $w$ coordinates, and quotient surjectivity and step 1 give equality of their constant coefficients. Therefore $\rho=\sigma$. Evaluate at $q(y_j)$ and subtract the constant series to obtain $\psi_j=\phi_j$.

MvPowerSeries.isUnit_iff_constantCoeff shows that every denominator outside the evaluation kernel is sent to a unit. Extend $\tau$ and $\sigma$ with IsLocalization.lift, and extend $q$ using Localization.localRingHom; all three maps have the asserted restrictions to the original rings. IsLocalization.ringHom_ext reduces equality of the two homomorphisms on the localized ambient ring to the comparison in step 3. The equations and uniqueness for localized equations follow by their restrictions to the original generators.

For a coefficient-field homomorphism $\iota:L\to K$, MvPowerSeries.map_subst says coefficientwise mapping commutes with substitution. Check separately the $W$ and $Y$ blocks, using map_X on the first block. Applying this identity to the localized comparison proves its coefficient compatibility. For the full comparison and uniqueness over $K$, apply step 3 to $\epsilon_K=\iota\epsilon$, $\tau_K=\iota_*\tau$ and $\sigma_K=\iota_*\sigma$. The mapAlgHom API, constantCoeff_map, map_add, map_C and map_X prove all required hypotheses, and mapping the explicit difference defining $\phi$ identifies the resulting graph vector with $\iota_*\phi$. This proves uniqueness for every zero-constant candidate over $K$, including candidates not defined over $L$.

The power-series Noetherian and local instances, the proper-kernel argument and all homomorphism APIs above admit zero variables. The quotient factorization uses the span of the image of Fin s and so also admits no generators. Consequently the same Lean proof handles $m=0$, $r=0$ and $s=0$. It uses neither maximality nor surjectivity of the field-valued evaluations and places no algebraicity condition on either coefficient field.

Étaleness is stated as RingHom.Etale of MvPolynomial.aeval for A and D, which brief-stage2 §3 allows. D and q are literally A⧸span(range h) and Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ. Constant-term and coordinate hypotheses hτ₀, hσ₀, hτw, hτy, hσw match, with castAdd as the W block and natAdd as the Y block. All conclusion clauses are present: zero constants of the graph vector, the comparison by genuine subst (HasSubst holds since all substituted series have zero constant term), the equations, uniqueness over all zero-constant ψ, the localized comparison through ring homs τₚ, σₚ, qₚ fixed by their restrictions, and the coefficient extension over every field K with uniqueness for every ψ over K. Edge cases m, r, s = 0, D = 0 and non-maximal evaluation kernels are covered. Universes u, v, w, x are independent. etaleGraphVector is an explicit formula and evaluationLocalization is Mathlib's Localization.AtPrime, so no hollow definitions.
